nodes.summary: WEIGHTED NUMBER OF TARDY JOBS is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of weighted tardy jobs instances, to a feasible instance, that is, an instance having an ordering of its jobs whose weighted number of tardy jobs is at most its bound. A bitstring that decodes to no instance is rejected.
nodes.title: The weighted number of tardy jobs decision problem

nodes.summary: A weighted tardy jobs instance, consisting of a list of $n$ jobs and a bound $K$, is feasible when there is an ordering of its jobs, that is, a list of the job indices $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$ in which each index occurs exactly once, whose weighted number of tardy jobs is at most $K$.
nodes.title: Feasible weighted tardy jobs instances

nodes.summary: An instance of WEIGHTED NUMBER OF TARDY JOBS is a pair consisting of a finite list of jobs, each a triple $(p, d, w)$ of natural numbers giving its processing time $p$, due date $d$ and weight $w$, and a natural number $K$, the bound.
nodes.title: Weighted tardy jobs instances

nodes.summary: The weighted number of tardy jobs decision problem lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: WEIGHTED NUMBER OF TARDY JOBS is NP-complete

nodes.summary: Let $J$ be a list of jobs, each a triple $(p, d, w)$ of natural numbers (processing time, due date, weight). Given a state $(t, s)$ and a natural number $j$, let $(p, d, w)$ be the job at position $j$ of $J$, counting from $0$, or $(0, 0, 0)$ if $J$ has no position $j$, and let $t' = t + p$. The step returns $(t', s + w)$ if $d < t'$, and $(t', s)$ otherwise.
nodes.title: One step of the weighted tardy jobs computation

nodes.summary: Let $J$ be a list of jobs, each a triple of natural numbers (processing time, due date, weight), and write $(p_i, d_i, w_i)$ for the job at position $i$ of $J$, counting from $0$, with $(p_i, d_i, w_i) = (0, 0, 0)$ when $J$ has no position $i$.
